facts.raw_span: A young girl initially came under care at age 4 years
developed an irregular brown-black patch on her left lateral ankle, measuring 3.6 × 3 cm
triangular hyperpigmented, asymptomatic patch consisting of confluent mottled black and brown macules and several satellite lesions
slow but progressive growth of the hyperpigmented patch, which had increased to 5.5 × 5-cm
two discrete areas of regression were noted
discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network were observed
No induration was palpated except at the previous biopsy site
Shows a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction consistent with an atypical compound nevus
Shows atypical nevus with areas of dermal fibrosis
Score: -7.1 (where scores from -16.7 to -2.1 are consistent with a benign nevus)
A large, dark brown patch consisting of coalescing macules and satellite lesions
The patch shows areas of regression on the medial and left upper borders

concepts.why: The presence of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes, bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, and areas of dermal fibrosis, along with the observation of regression, supports this diagnosis.
The gene expression testing score of -7.1, which is consistent with a benign nevus, along with the clinical presentation of a hyperpigmented patch with satellite lesions, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of a large, hyperpigmented patch with satellite lesions, which has been present since childhood and has shown slow growth, supports this diagnosis.
It explains the dermoscopic finding of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network.

rationales.F02: The presence of an irregular brown-black patch is more typical of atypical melanocytic nevus and congenital melanocytic nevus.
rationales.F03: The description of a triangular hyperpigmented patch with confluent mottled black and brown macules and satellite lesions is more characteristic of atypical melanocytic nevus and congenital melanocytic nevus.
rationales.F04: The slow but progressive growth of the hyperpigmented patch is more typical of atypical melanocytic nevus and congenital melanocytic nevus.
rationales.F06: The dermoscopic features of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas with gray-brown structureless areas and a negative pigment network are highly suggestive of atypical melanocytic nevus.
rationales.F08: The histopathological features of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction are consistent with an atypical compound nevus, which is a type of atypical melanocytic nevus.
rationales.F10: The gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, which decreases the likelihood of atypical melanocytic nevus.

frontier_selector.rationale: Histopathology findings of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with areas of dermal fibrosis and random nuclear atypia, support the diagnosis of an atypical melanocytic nevus, despite a gene expression test score consistent with a benign nevus.
